questions.title: Term for a darkly stained shrunken nucleus
questions.question: Which of the following term best describes the darkly stained shrunken nucleus?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A hypersensitivity reaction is an immune response category, not a term for a nuclear morphological change.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Inflammatory reaction describes a tissue-level response to injury, not the specific nuclear appearance being asked about.
explanations.C: Correct. Pyknosis is the term for the nucleus of a necrotic cell shrinking and staining more darkly (more deeply basophilic/condensed) — one of the three recognised nuclear changes of necrosis, alongside karyolysis (fading of nuclear basophilia) and karyorrhexis (destructive fragmentation, which follows pyknosis). "Darkly stained and shrunken" is precisely the descriptive definition of pyknosis, distinguishing it from karyolysis (fading, not darkening) and karyorrhexis (fragmentation, not simple shrinkage).
explanations.D: Incorrect. Karyorrhexis is destructive fragmentation of the nucleus, which follows pyknosis rather than describing the darkly stained, shrunken stage itself.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Karyolysis is the fading of nuclear basophilia (the nucleus becoming paler), the opposite direction of change from a darkly stained nucleus.

questions.learning_objective: Name pyknosis as the term for a darkly stained, shrunken nucleus, distinguishing it from karyorrhexis and karyolysis.
